title: PowerRChol: Efficient Power Grid Analysis Based on Fast Randomized Cholesky Factorization
problem: Power grid analysis requires solving large linear equations with millions of unknowns, which is computationally challenging. Existing preconditioning approaches suffer from either high construction costs or slow convergence rates, resulting in unsatisfactory total solution time.
motivation: Efficient power grid analysis is critical for modern VLSI design.
method: PowerRChol proposes a randomized Cholesky factorization algorithm with provable linear-time complexity to serve as a preconditioner for iterative solvers. It incorporates a randomized factorization oriented matrix reordering approach to optimize memory access patterns and solver convergence. The method integrates with Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient (PCG) solvers to efficiently solve sparse linear systems arising from power grid analysis.
key_novelty: Fast randomized Cholesky factorization with provable linear-time complexity that overcomes the high construction cost and slow convergence limitations of existing preconditioning approaches.
contributions: Randomized Cholesky factorization algorithm with provable linear-time complexity for efficient preconditioning
Randomized factorization oriented matrix reordering approach to optimize solver performance
Demonstrated superior efficiency achieving 1.51X, 1.93X, and 3.64X speedups over RChol, feGRASS, and AMG based solvers respectively
Practical validation on large-scale power grids with 60 million nodes and 260 million nonzeros
